record.original_question: Fix a possibly infinite collection of affine constraints {(M_1,sigma_1),(M_2,sigma_2),...} over F2. For each n, let P_n be the property that a function f : F2^n -> {0,1} is (M_i,sigma_i)-free for every i. Must there exist a one-sided-error constant-query property-testing algorithm for P_n?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let M in F2^{m x k} and sigma in {0, 1}^k. Say that f : F2^n -> {0, 1} is (M, sigma)-free if there does not exist X = ( x^(1), ..., x^(k) ) such that M X = 0 and f ( x^(j) ) = sigma_j for all j in [ k]. Now fix a possibly infinite collection {( M_1 , sigma_1 ), ( M_2 , sigma_2 ), ...} and consider the property P_n of functions f : F2^n -> {0, 1} that f is ( M_i , sigma_i )-free for all i. Then there is a one-sided error, constant-query property-testing algorithm for P_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the field $\mathbb{F}_2$. For a matrix $M \in \mathbb{F}_2^{m \times k}$ and a vector $\sigma \in \{0,1\}^k$, say that a function $f : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{0,1\}$ is $(M,\sigma)$-free if there do not exist vectors $x^{(1)}, \ldots, x^{(k)} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that
\[ M\,(x^{(1)}, \ldots, x^{(k)})^\top = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad f(x^{(j)}) = \sigma_j \text{ for all } j \in [k]. \]
Fix any (possibly infinite) collection $\{(M_1,\sigma_1),(M_2,\sigma_2),\ldots\}$ where $M_i \in \mathbb{F}_2^{m_i \times k_i}$ and $\sigma_i \in \{0,1\}^{k_i}$. For each $n$, let $P_n$ be the property of functions $f : \mathbb{F}_2^n \to \{0,1\}$ defined by: $f \in P_n$ iff $f$ is $(M_i,\sigma_i)$-free for every $i$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a one-sided-error, constant-query property tester for $P_n$. That is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant $q = q(\varepsilon)$ and a randomized algorithm that queries $f$ on at most $q$ points, accepts with probability $1$ when $f \in P_n$, and rejects with probability at least $2/3$ when $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far (in Hamming distance, normalized) from $P_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Bhattacharyya, Chen, Sudan and Xie) was resolved positively by Asaf Shapira, who proved that every (possibly infinite) system of linear/affine equations over a finite abelian group has the removal property, which implies that the family of $(M_i,\sigma_i)$-free properties is testable with one-sided error and a constant number of queries. Independent/related resolutions were also obtained by Král', Serra, and Vena.

status_evidence.title: Green's Conjecture and Testing Linear Invariant Properties
status_evidence.snippet: Shapira confirmed Green's conjecture by showing that every set of linear equations has the removal property; this resolves a conjecture of Bhattacharyya, Chen, Sudan and Xie on testing properties of Boolean functions.

status_evidence.title: Green's Conjecture and Testing Linear Invariant Properties (SpringerLink)
status_evidence.snippet: The result resolves the conjecture of Bhattacharyya, Chen, Sudan and Xie regarding testing of Boolean functions for being (M,sigma)-free.
